item.title: Kanuma Autumn Festival: Carved Floats & a Curious 'Butcher's' Nickname — Guide
item.description: The Kanuma Autumn Festival, designated a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage alongside 32 other Japanese float festivals, showcases roughly 27 elaborately carved wooden floats (yatai) built by craftsmen whose woodworking skills trace back to artisans who worked on nearby Nikko Toshogu shrine centuries ago. The festival’s English nickname, ‘Butcher’s Festival,’ is a quirky mistranslation of ‘Bukkake Matsuri’ (referring to the festival’s energetic float-pulling style), and today it draws large crowds each October to see the floats paraded through Kanuma’s streets accompanied by traditional music.
